chunks: And from him, from Abu Ishaq, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I was with him when a man came and asked him. He said: 'A man divorced his wife three times.' The Imam said: 'She is divorced from him.' The man left. Then another man from our companions came and said: 'A man divorced his wife three times.' The Imam said: 'One divorce.' Another came and said: 'A man divorced his wife three times.' The Imam said: 'It is nothing.' Then he looked at me and said: 'It is as you see.'

I said: 'How is this?' He said: 'This one thinks that whoever divorces his wife three times, she becomes forbidden to him. But I think that whoever divorces his wife three times in accordance with the Sunnah, she is divorced from him. And if a man divorces his wife three times while she is in a state of purity, it is only one divorce. And if a man divorces his wife three times while she is not in a state of purity, it is nothing.'

key_terms.عَلَى غَيْرِ طُهْرٍ: not in a state of purity

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on triple divorce if done in accordance with the Sunnah versus during menstruation?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the concept of *Tafwid* (delegation) in triple divorce, distinguishing between divorces performed in accordance with the Sunnah versus those done in haste or during menstruation. It highlights the jurisprudential nuance that a triple divorce pronounced while the wife is in a state of purity (*Tahur*) is treated as a single irrevocable divorce, whereas one pronounced during menstruation is considered invalid or 'nothing,' contrasting with the view that any triple divorce immediately causes permanent separation. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the quality and timing of the divorce act rather than merely the number of utterances.
